pages.text: Each mineral is stable only in part of the pressure-temperature plane, and the lines between them follow the Clapeyron slope dP/dT = ΔS/ΔV. Hold the sample on the right side of the line and keep it hot enough to react: the rate follows Arrhenius, e^(−Eₐ/RT).
$(thing)Set$(): Anvil pressure P, Furnace temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Gasket creep: the sample sees P·(1 ± 2%·d).
$(thing)Limits$(): Tungsten-carbide anvils deforming above 26 GPa; The press frame is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Hotter samples react faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sample pressure: P_s = P·(1 + 0.02·d)$(br)Equivalent depth: z = P/(ρg)$(br)Graphite-diamond line: P = 1.94 + 0.0025·T(°C)$(br)Ringwoodite line: P = 17.5 + 0.005·(T − 1873)$(br)Post-spinel line: P = 23.5 − 0.0025·(T − 1900)$(br)Margin over the diamond line: P − P_dg$(br)Margin over the ringwoodite line: P − P_rw
